settings.sec.usercfg.desc: The SCDL creates a user.cfg in each Star Citizen installation folder if there is none yet. If one already exists, it checks whether g_language = german_(germany) and g_languageAudio = english are set, and adds them if they are missing. The German language slot is only the carrier, not the content: Star Citizen offers no free slot for custom language files, so the SCDL puts every translation there – an Italian or Japanese one too. bp.helpModal.body:
This module marks your earned blueprints directly in the game: [x] (already earned) and [ ] (still open) will appear next to each blueprint in mission texts. There are two ways to import your collection.

METHOD 1Log ScannerFully automatic, but error-prone

The log scanner reads your Star Citizen log files and detects all earned blueprints without any manual input.

1
When you receive a blueprint, Star Citizen writes the entry Bauplan erhalten: into the log files. When the game closes, this file is automatically backed up to logbackups/.
2
The SCDL monitors the current log files in the installation directory while Star Citizen is running. As soon as Star Citizen writes a blueprint entry, it is detected within ~2 seconds and added to the collection without interrupting gameplay. Note: The [x] marker in mission texts will only appear after the next game start, as Star Citizen loads its texts into memory only on startup.
3
All found blueprints are merged with the existing collection and immediately injected into all active Star Citizen installations. A banner with the result will appear in the SCDL.
4
On SCDL start, once you have used the log scan at least once, a full scan of all log files (Game.log + logbackups/) is automatically run so no blueprints earned in the meantime are missed.
Manual scan: Use Import from log files to start a full scan of all log files at any time, for example during initial setup.
Scanned directories:
StarCitizen\LIVE\Game.log
StarCitizen\LIVE\logbackups\*.log
StarCitizen\HOTFIX\Game.log
StarCitizen\HOTFIX\logbackups\*.log
PTU/EPTU are not included. Blueprints are collected across installations in sc_bp_erledigt.json for LIVE/HOTFIX.
Tip: As long as you keep your log files, you can run the scan again at any time across multiple game sessions. Already imported blueprints are stored in sc_bp_erledigt.json regardless, even if you delete old log backups later.
METHOD 2Import via Blueprint DBManual · full control
1
To mark your scanned blueprints as earned, open our blueprint database sc-deutsch-launcher.de/blueprints in your browser.
2
Mark each earned blueprint by clicking the symbol, and the name lights up green:
Blueprint item
3
Click Export in the top right → select Earned as JSON:
Export
→ Earned as JSON
Bookmarked as JSON
All as JSON / CSV
The file is saved as sc_bp_erledigt.json.
4
Click Import from JSON file in the SCDL and select the saved file. The blueprints are immediately imported and injected into all active Star Citizen installations.
In-game display:
After importing, [x] (earned) and [ ] (still open) will appear next to each blueprint in mission texts. Thanks to Auto-Sync, your markers are automatically transferred to the new global.ini with every language update. You do not need to repeat anything by hand.

Note: Star Citizen loads its texts into memory only on game start. New [x] markers will not be visible in a running game session, but only after the next Star Citizen start.

gt.modal.title: Game statistics
gt.nav.intro: Reads the log files of your installation. The scan only runs when you start it.
gt.leer: The log files say nothing about this.
gt.scan.title: Scan
gt.scan.desc: This is where the statistics come from. The scan only runs when you press the button. Files already read are remembered, so next time only the new ones are scanned.
gt.scan.hinweis: Star Citizen keeps only the most recent log files and deletes older ones itself. The launcher therefore stores a summary on every run. Sessions once read stay in your statistics even after the file is gone.
gt.scan.abJahr: Only log files from 2026 onwards are read. Star Citizen changed its log messages several times across builds: older files miss messages entirely or word them in a way today's reader misreads. Numbers from 2025 and earlier would look right without being right — hence the cut. Older files already read are removed again on the next scan. Playtime is not affected and counts all log files, including older ones.
gt.auto.desc: Reads new log files without a button press: about 90 seconds after each game start and once shortly after the launcher starts. Only new files are read.
gt.stats.nochNichts: Nothing scanned yet. Run the scan and your numbers appear here.
gt.namen.fehlt: Ship and weapon names still show as class codes: the blueprint catalog hasn't been downloaded yet.
gt.namen.kaputt: Ship and weapon names show as class codes: the blueprint catalog could not be read.
gt.waffen.hinweis: Based on attachment log events, not an exact carry/shot statistic.
gt.schiffeVerloren.hinweis: Counted when you are ejected from a destroyed ship. A ship destroyed without you on board is not in the log.
gt.sess.title: Stability
gt.sess.desc: How often the game exited cleanly, how often it crashed, and why the connection dropped.
gt.sess.kontoweit: This page always covers all characters together, including the session list. A session ends, not a character – the log does not tie the ending to a name. That is why there is no selector here.
gt.sess.abbruchHinweis: These are disconnects from the game server (<Channel Disconnected> in the log), not abandoned missions — those are in the Missions area. Every server change creates one entry, so an evening easily reaches a dozen. Server changes and disconnecting yourself are normal operation, not a fault.
gt.tab.name: Name
gt.heat.hinweis: The brighter, the more playtime. A session across midnight counts proportionally in both hours, not entirely in the starting hour.
gt.zone.zeit.hinweis: Time per jurisdiction is counted from entering one until entering the next — the game does not report leaving. The last jurisdiction of a session is therefore not counted.
gt.schiffe.verlauf.sub: One point per month with an ASOP terminal opened ({0} in total). Months without a visit are missing.
gt.qt.title: Quantum travel
gt.qt.desc: Every target selection and every arrival is in the log. They are paired by ship – travel time only counts for a jump that has both.
gt.qt.hinweis: Destinations and departure points appear as location keys in the log ('rs_asmbl_keeger_02'). There is no name catalogue for them – they stay exactly as the game writes them.
gt.qt.treibstoff.hinweis: The value is the quantum drive's estimate before the jump, not the fuel actually burned.
gt.miss.title: Missions
gt.miss.desc: What was accepted, completed and abandoned – plus objectives and, where the log names it, the payout.
gt.miss.hinweis: The mission type comes from the internal contract code and is the same in every game language. Ø duration counts finished missions only, and objectives only those the game actually shows. Party data only exists for logs analyzed with this version – for older logs use “Rescan everything”.
gt.miss.belohnung.hinweis: The payout appears as a separate notification without a mission id; it is matched by how close it is to the mission ending. It shows up in only a small share of log files – the total is therefore not your overall earnings. Event missions often pay no aUEC at all.
gt.zone.title: Jurisdictions and zones
gt.zone.desc: The game reports entering and leaving in plain text. Both together give the time spent.
gt.zone.hinweis: These notifications appear in the language Star Citizen itself runs in – German and English are recognised. If a leave message is missing (server change, crash), that stay is not counted.
gt.schiffe.title: Ships, fleet and gear
gt.schiffe.desc: Which ship was in use, how large your own fleet is and what you actually put on.
gt.schiffe.flotte.leer: no ASOP terminal in the logs
gt.schiffe.flotte.hinweis: Fleet size only appears in the log when an ASOP terminal was opened. Without that it stays empty.
gt.med.title: Injuries and medical
gt.med.desc: Star Citizen reports injuries, being incapacitated and medical bed use in plain text.
gt.med.hinweis: A documented substitute for the death detection that disappeared: being incapacitated and using a medical bed are real messages, not an estimate. They too follow the game's language – German and English are recognised.
gt.leeren.frage: Really clear the cache? Everything it holds will be lost: statistics, missions, ships and all other evaluations. Star Citizen deletes old log files on its own – their values only live in the cache and will be gone for good. A new scan only finds the logs that are still there. Back them up first with Profile Backup (group "Game statistics").
gt.leeren.spielzeit.desc: Total playtime stays as it is, including hours from deleted logs and a value you entered by hand. When off, it starts at zero and only counts the logs that are still there.

si.pane.noPath: No install path is set for this channel. Once it is set in the settings, its data appears here.
si.sec.perf.desc: The CPU index measures the main thread (game logic, AI, physics), the GPU index the render thread (pixels, draw calls, shading). Both come from a short benchmark at game start.
si.pi.cpuHint: Measures a short, sequential benchmark at startup – without a loaded game world. It does not reflect performance during gameplay.
si.pi.x3dHint: 3D V-Cache CPUs often show lower values than expected here – the benefit of their large cache only shows during gameplay in dense scenes.
si.pi.gpuHint: Depends on the resolution – the same GPU scores much lower at 4K than at 1080p.
si.pi.compare: CPU and GPU index measure different things and cannot be compared directly. A lower GPU value does not necessarily mean the GPU is the bottleneck – at a different resolution the ratio would change.
si.val.ram: {0} GB installed, ~{1}% in use at startup

joysticks.analyse.desc: Checks bindings, Game.log and input devices and builds a report you can share on Discord. Your user name and personal paths are removed. The input test guides you step by step: press a button, hands off, move the sticks.

joysticks.analyse.tasten.text: Press every button and hat switch once, flip switches too. “Done” ends early.
joysticks.analyse.wecken.text: Press any button on every device. Windows only reports a device after its first input. If one is missing, “Skip step” goes on without it.

bindings.title: Bindings
bindings.desc: All game actions with their bindings. Green marks what the selected file binds itself, yellow what is not saved yet; everything else is the game's default. Click a binding to rebind it, right-click to clear it or restore the game default. Click a group name to collapse it. Names and keys come from the language set in the game.

bindings.zuo.desc: After a restart or a port change Windows sometimes numbers joysticks differently, and bindings then sit on the wrong device. Remember the order while everything is right. After every game session the SCDL compares it with the Game.log and reports differences.
bindings.zuo.export: The joystick order only applies to the active game bindings. In the “Bindings” tab, choose actionmaps.xml as the file.

bindings.zuo.status.log-unlesbar: The Game.log exists but could not be read ({0}). Quit Star Citizen and check again.
bindings.zuo.status.ok: The order of the last session matches the remembered one.
bindings.zuo.status.geaendert: The order has changed. "Adjust bindings" puts every binding back on its device.

geraete.hilfe: Re-detect devices or ignore a device in SCDL. An ignored device no longer provides input here. Star Citizen and other programs are not affected. To hide a device from Star Citizen as well, a tool such as HidHide is needed.
geraete.hidhideText: If a device is missing or only partly detected, HidHide is often the reason. After a Windows restart or a USB port change, Windows can give the device a new ID and the HidHide rule no longer applies: select the device again in HidHide. Windows also registers Xbox controllers in two ways, and HidHide does not always hide both. Afterwards use “Re-detect devices” here.

geraete.ignoriertToast: The device is ignored in SCDL until it is disconnected or the launcher restarts. Star Citizen still sees it.

il.nav.intro: The bar follows every change right away. While this window is open you see it as a preview.
il.icon.desc: Whether the overlay gets its own icon in the title bar. Hiding it does not switch the module off.

il.scan.desc: Reads the signature (RS value) from the screen in scanning mode and shows what is behind it: rocks with their count, salvage panels, wreck debris or ground deposits. Reading only happens on a key press, a controller button or a click on the radar button in the overlay, using the Windows text recognition.
il.scan.taste.aktiv: Active. The shortcut only applies while Star Citizen is running.
il.scan.taste.belegt: Another program already uses this shortcut. Please choose a different one.

il.scan.dlg.kombiFrei: The combination is free in the game. The key itself is bound with other modifiers, which does not interfere.

il.scan.tabelle.kaputt: The signature table is damaged and is not used. The next catalogue sync downloads it again.
il.scan.fehler.plattform: Text recognition is only available on Windows
il.scan.fehler.bereich: Scan area invalid – please select it again
il.scan.fehler.sprache: Windows has no text recognition installed (English language pack with “Optical character recognition”)
il.scan.fehler.auto: Automatic reading paused: text recognition does not start. Details in the activity log.
il.scan.ctrl.hinweis: Only works while Star Citizen is running and an area is selected. The button keeps its function in the game – ideally pick a free one.
il.scan.kd.titel: Controller button for the signature scan
il.scan.kd.text: Press the button you want on your gamepad or joystick. Clicking the field waits for a new button. Esc cancels.
il.scan.kd.istGp: That was a gamepad – this sets a joystick button.
il.scan.kd.istJs: That was a joystick – this sets a gamepad button.
il.scan.kd.ersetzt: The scan uses one controller button: {0} will be replaced.
il.scan.kd.ohneKennung: This device reports no ID and cannot be assigned. Please use another button or device.
il.scan.probe.nichts: No signature recognised – there was no text in the area.
il.schirm.hinweis: Click a field in the picture to set the position.
il.scan.schirm.hinweis: Orange: the area read by text recognition.
il.scan.bereit: Ready. Press {0} in scanning mode – the result appears in the overlay.
il.scan.nichtBereit.bereich: Not ready yet: first select the area around the signature number.
il.scan.nichtBereit.ausloeser: Not ready yet: set a trigger. Until then, only the radar button in the overlay scans.
il.scan.ausloeser.hinweis: Shortcuts, buttons and automatic reading only work while Star Citizen is running and an area is selected.
il.scan.art.tastatur.desc: A keyboard shortcut, e.g. Ctrl + Shift + S.
il.scan.art.gamepad.desc: A button on an Xbox-compatible gamepad. It keeps its function in the game – ideally pick a free one.
il.scan.art.joystick.desc: A button on a joystick or throttle. It keeps its function in the game – ideally pick a free one.
il.scan.art.auto.desc: Reads the area every second while Star Citizen is running and only reports new signatures. As long as the image does not change, it uses hardly any CPU.
il.scan.bereit.auto: Ready. In scanning mode SCDL reads the signature every second by itself – the result appears in the overlay.
il.scan.bereit.autoZusatz: It also reads every second by itself.
il.set.klickDurch.desc: Mouse clicks go through the bar to the game. When disabled, a click on the pill keeps the detail view open.
il.set.nurSc.desc: The bar only appears while Star Citizen runs. When disabled, it also shows the last session without the game.
il.set.hinweise.desc: New events briefly appear as a notice below the pill.
il.set.hervorheben.desc: The pill lights up when you leave an armistice zone, get injured, die or lose the connection.
il.set.icon.desc: Shows an icon in the title bar that opens these settings. When disabled, you still reach them through the module card in the settings.
